title: Second largest eigenvalue does not bound stationary entropy production
abstract: We examine the spectral dissipation-coherence trade-off inequality conjectured by Oberreiter {\it et al}. [Phys. Rev. E 106, 014106 (2022)], stating that the coherent number, defined from the second largest eigenvalue, provides a lower bound on the stationary entropy production per unit oscillation. We disprove this conjecture by explicitly constructing a counterexample, which accompanies finite coherent number with vanishing stationary entropy production. This model also excludes a wide class of thermodynamic bound with the real and imaginary parts of the second largest eigenvalue of the transition rate matrix. Our result implies that the second largest eigenvalue does not necessarily characterize the degree of coherent oscillation.
summary: This theoretical paper constructs a counterexample to the spectral dissipation-coherence trade-off inequality in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics. By analyzing a specific three-layer Markov process, the authors show that the stationary entropy production can vanish while the second largest eigenvalue remains finite. This result implies that the second largest eigenvalue does not universally bound the thermodynamic cost of coherent oscillations.
main_problem: The paper aims to disprove the spectral dissipation-coherence trade-off (DCT) inequality, which conjectures that stationary entropy production is bounded below by a quantity derived from the second largest eigenvalue.
main_result: The authors construct a counterexample model where the stationary entropy production vanishes while the second largest eigenvalue remains finite, thereby disproving the conjectured bound.
method: The analysis involves constructing a specific Markov jump process on a lattice and calculating the stationary entropy production ($\sigma_{ss}$) and the second largest eigenvalue ($\lambda_2$) using master equation formalism.
model_or_system: The system is a Markov jump process modeled by a transition rate matrix $R$ acting on three coupled layers (A, B, C) arranged in one-dimensional lattices with periodic boundary conditions.
key_observables: Stationary entropy production ($\sigma_{ss}$), Coherent Number ($N$), and the second largest eigenvalue ($\lambda_2$) characterized by its real ($\lambda_R$) and imaginary ($\lambda_I$) parts.
important_parameters: The small parameter $\epsilon = 1/L^q$ is crucial, as the counterexample shows $\sigma_{ss} \propto \epsilon$ while $\lambda_R$ remains $O(1)$.
main_assumptions: The conjecture was previously supported by numerical simulations and proven in specific regimes, but the counterexample shows the bound fails generally.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the three-layer model (A, B, C) and the cyclic driving mechanism connecting the layers.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the spectral DCT inequality, presents the specific three-layer counterexample model, calculates the required observables ($\sigma_{ss}$ and $\lambda_2$), and finally demonstrates the violation of the inequality in the limit $\epsilon 	o 0$.
why_interesting: This work challenges fundamental, seemingly universal bounds in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, suggesting that spectral properties alone are insufficient to characterize thermodynamic costs like entropy production.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of our model disproving the spectral DCT inequality. Our model consists of three layers, A, B, and C, which are one-dimensional with L sites with the peri- odic boundary condition. The state of the system is specified by (i, a) with site 1 ≤i ≤L and layer a ∈{A, B, C}. In a single jump, the site changes as i →i±1 in the same layer, or the layer changes in the same site. Layer A has small nonequi- librium driving, while layers B and C have no driving. In a single site, we have nonequilibrium driving in the direction A →B →C →A. The stationary probability of layer A is extremely small (of order O(ε2)).
